risks.risk: Item may not be a complete engine; could be engine mounting parts/insulators only, so pricing for an engine would be wrong.
risks.proof: Ask for a photo showing the full engine (engine block + cylinder head) with engine ID/plate and a clear view of the starter/alternator area.
risks.if_unproven: Price as used engine-mounting parts (worst case: worn/rusty and not guaranteed for fit), not as a working engine.

risks.proof: Ask for the vehicle details the engine/mounts came from (make/model/year/engine code) and a photo of any stamped part numbers.
risks.if_unproven: Price at the lowest compatible/unknown-fit assumption (worst case: may not fit).

risks.risk: Condition risk: rubber bushings/insulators may be cracked, hardened, or torn; rust may indicate water ingress or long storage.
risks.proof: Ask for close-up photos of each rubber bushing/insulator (front and back) and any cracks/tears, plus a photo of the mounting surfaces.
risks.if_unproven: Price as worn parts needing replacement (worst case: not serviceable).

risks.risk: Seller claim of 'no knock/low mileage/never opened' cannot be verified because no engine is shown.
risks.proof: Ask for a short video of the engine running (cold start if possible) and a sound recording, plus compression test or diagnostic report.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not proven working (worst case: treat as non-working/unknown).

proof_requests: Confirm exactly what is for sale: complete engine vs engine mounting parts. Send photos of the full engine (if it is an engine).
Provide engine ID/plate or stamped numbers (clear close-up) and the vehicle make/model/year it came from.
If it’s mounts/insulators: send close-ups of every rubber bushing/insulator showing cracks/tears and the mounting bolt holes.
Send a video proof of testing/running (if an engine): start-up + idle + brief rev, plus any diagnostic/compression results.
